The complete 2D generator configures the pinned FastNoiseLite 1.1.0 algorithms, exposes all applicable settings and numeric modes, and emits the observed resource notifications. C++ reference vectors, copying and NoiseTexture integration pass in FastNoiseLiteTests; Vector2 offset preserves XY only. Retained Sprite pixels pass on Linux Wayland compatibility and GPU backends; other platforms remain unchecked.
Three-dimensional noise samples and image volumes are outside the strict 2D product boundary (ADR 0004).
The vector overload delegates coordinates to the concrete 2D sampler; NoiseTests checks dispatch and disposed access.

The 2D path samples a concrete subclass into L8, supports normalization, inversion and finite-value rejection in NoiseTests. The 3D-space option is excluded; exact large-value pixel parity and a concrete built-in sampler remain to verify.

The 2D overlap/quadrant blend executes for L8 and RGBA8 and is checked in NoiseTests. Pixel-for-pixel parity for arbitrary skirts and derived source formats remains unverified; the 3D-space option is excluded.
Input.MouseModeEnum has exact pinned values; the Enum suffix is required by the C# MouseMode property. Native Wayland tests verify the five selectable modes.
All 17 cursor identities match the pinned values. Native Wayland tests select every shape and verify Input observes direct DisplayServer changes.
Input delegates read/write to the active DisplayServer. Native Wayland tests verify all five selectable modes, SDL relative/grab/visibility state, repeated setting and no-host failure.

Image and readable Texture pixels are copied into an SDL cursor with per-shape slots, size/hotspot validation and null reset; native tests cover Image and errors. AnimatedTexture first-frame semantics and other backends remain unaudited.

Stores the viewport default separately from the current native shape and refreshes hovered Control overrides immediately. The pinned synthetic mouse-motion event on default changes and complete nested viewport GUI routing remain absent.
Finite coordinates truncate to native client pixels and delegate to DisplayServer; Wayland correctly rejects unsupported warp. Supported backend movement/clipping has not been natively verified.
Borrowed catalog registration, identity deduplication, snapshot query, removal and disposal were checked in TranslationDomainTests; returned arrays are independent.

The domain stores the pinned defaults and typed setter values; TranslationDomainTests checks configuration and lookup effects. BIDI and Unicode transform fidelity is classified on pseudolocalize itself.
Executable domain lookup, override and parent-culture fallback are tested; exact upstream locale scoring, normalization and plural-rule parity remain unaudited.
Singular transforms and expansion are executable and tested, but exact code-point, placeholder, BIDI and expansion rounding parity remains unaudited.

Counts contextual entries, returns EOT-prefixed context keys and flattens every translated plural form into independent arrays; VerifyTranslations checks each operation. Enumeration order is unspecified in both hash-backed catalogs.

Generate creates an in-memory hash-keyed Brotli catalog, discards source text and contextual entries, resolves singular compressed values and duplicates independently. VerifyTranslations covers lookup, registration, copying, empty generation and disposal. The pinned Smaz binary representation, editor-only generation gate and asset-file persistence are absent; the shared runtime/editor assembly currently permits explicit generation at runtime.
The managed state transition and empty/valid results were compared with the pinned implementation and tested.
The result retains the full original source string, including when end limits matching.
The .NET dialect differs from the pinned PCRE2 dialect; named capture ordering/duplicates and malformed-pattern behavior need parity work. Managed exceptions replace numeric errors.
Search and replacement execute, but .NET syntax, replacement tokens and UTF-16 positions differ from PCRE2/code-point behavior.
Typed int/string accessors work, but .NET group numbering for mixed captures, duplicate names and UTF-16 positions need PCRE2/code-point parity.
